comments.body:
**Escalating to Secure / Incident Engineering.** Matt Kamminga was working this with me and is out until 2026-10-05. The ticket is High and the resolution SLA is breached.

## 1. Environment and steps to reproduce

**Environment: Production.** Tenant `209-tbi`, Tailored Brands. Web role `web-prd-wus2-arp-nettrack`.

1. Sign in to Secure as a Tailored Brands user.
2. Open Incident from Secure. The transition lands on `SystemSelect.aspx`.
3. Time the transition from the click until the page renders.

Expected: not documented. Support holds no target load time for this path. Actual: 35 to 40 seconds, Colton Neal, 2026-09-16. These are customer timings from the ticket comments. No screenshot of the load time exists.

| Date | Customer timing |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-08-12 | 30 to 45 s, three users |
| 2026-09-02 | 30 to 40 s |
| 2026-09-16 | 35 to 40 s |

## 2. Findings

1. ENG-7168 <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-7168</custom>  shipped on 2026-08-27. **The customer timings did not change across that release.**
2. I read the Incident flags in production on 2026-09-08. The two AdHoc flags and `EnableScreenLabelCaching` resolve `True`. `EnableBlobAppendLogging` resolves `False`. Detail and ruled out items are in my internal note of 2026-09-08 on this ticket.
3. Matt, Teams, 2026-09-24: "there is something odd going on for Tailored brands on that. I was in thier site trying to investigate but was not able to get to the bottom of it yet"
4. Precedent, not tested on 209: Chris Rippingale noted on ENG-7168 on 2026-08-14 that tenant 209 had a p50 of 78.8 s on AdHoc requests, higher than other tenants, and left a tenant specific problem as an open branch.

## 3. Troubleshooting and limits of support access

**AI use.** Claude consolidated the ticket history, cross read ENG-7168 and ENG-6680 <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-6680</custom> , and flagged a tenant specific problem on 209 as the likely open branch. I checked the flags in production myself, the ENG-7168 release in Jira, and the customer timings against the release date. My reading is that the remaining time sits outside screen label caching and the AdHoc flags on this tenant. Could someone with Profiler access evaluate this and share your thoughts?

**Conversations outside this ticket.** Matt Kamminga on Teams, 2026-09-24, quoted above. No other calls or channels since my note of 2026-09-08.

**What support cannot see.** Application Insights Profiler traces for tenant 209. Support has not timed the transition from a Tailored Brands session. Every timing above comes from the customer.

## 4. Open questions

1. Could someone look at Profiler traces for tenant 209 on the Secure to Incident transition?
2. What is the intended value of `Feature.Incident.EnableBlobAppendLogging` on 209?
3. Who could own this ticket while Matt is out?

**Update on the user access part, with a proposal to split this ticket.** The blank Incident Security ID and blank Hierarchy reports trace to two causes. Neither is limited to the six users reported here.

## 1. Environment and steps to reproduce

Production, tenant 209 tbi, `sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform`. Every query below is read only and was run on 2026-10-14.

### Rachel Dill, reported 2026-10-13

1. Rachel signs in through Okta SSO. `sso.ResponseLog` Id 30893, 2026-10-13 19:23:49 UTC.
2. Portal, Settings, Users, Rachel Dill, Secure Incident tab.

Expected: Incident Security ID Location Manager. `sso.SecurityLevelAssignments` has SecurityID 5 from the 2026-10-13 10:42 load, and `EXEC sso.GetUserSecurityLevel` returns 5 for her. Actual: Incident Security ID blank. `membership.Users.SecurityID` was NULL after that sign in. I set it to Location Manager manually on 2026-10-14.

### Chris Orth, reported 2026-10-12

1. Chris signs in on 2026-10-12 19:50 UTC, after Location Manager was applied to him manually.
2. He tries to create an incident.

Expected: he can select his store. Actual: error, and his Hierarchy page is blank. The feed sends him LocationID 90002005. That ID does not exist in `place.Location`, and he has no row in `secure.LocationHierarchyUserAssignments`.

## 2. Findings

| # | Finding | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 46 users who signed in since 2026-07-02 have a feed level above 0 and `membership.Users.SecurityID` NULL | verified |
| 2 | None of the 46 has a row in `incident.LPUser2`, by IncidentUserID or by LoginID and email | verified |
| 3 | With an LPUser2 row, 79 of 79 users have the level. Without one, 101 have it and 46 do not | verified |
| 4 | Christi Winters has a Persistent 1 level row from 2026-04-17, signed in 2026-07-14, and her account is still NULL | verified |
| 5 | 287 ApprissCase Users get a 9000xxxx LocationID in `sso.LocationHierarchyMembers` that is not in `place.Location` | verified |
| 6 | Latest rows in both SSO tables are from 2026-10-13 10:42. No 2026-10-14 load as of 18:57 UTC | verified |

`sso.GetUserSecurityLevel` shows modify_date 2026-10-09 09:11. The current definition orders by Persistent and has no Persistent = 1 filter. The SAML claims in `sso.ResponseLog` carry location and Okta group, with no team or level.

**My reading, unverified:** the step that copies the level to the account at sign in does not apply it for part of the users without an LPUser2 row. I do not know what separates the 101 from the 46. Some of the 101 were set manually.

## 3. Troubleshooting performed

In order: feed rows for the six users, account level against `incident.LPUser2` by both join routes as in <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-0">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-7189</custom> , the definition and output of `sso.GetUserSecurityLevel`, LastLoginDate, SAML claims, and LHUA plus `sso.LocationHierarchyMembers` against `place.Location`.

Applied today: Location Manager for Paul Bubelnik Jr, Nancy Bolhoff and Rachel Dill. Chaz Hyman, Vincent Fortner and Chris Orth already had level 5.

Outside the ticket: J.R. Teagle's email thread "Secure Incident ID, Choose a Value" asked for a review of <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-1">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-27269</custom> , <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-2">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-27578</custom> , <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-3">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/RCS-27941</custom>  and this ticket. I sent a Teams message to Matthew Kamminga on 2026-10-14.

```sql
SELECT ruta,nivel,COUNT(*) n FROM (SELECT CASE WHEN a.UserID IS NOT NULL THEN 'por ID' WHEN b.UserID IS NOT NULL THEN 'solo por email o login' ELSE 'ninguna' END ruta,CASE WHEN u.SecurityID IS NULL THEN 'cuenta NULL' ELSE 'con nivel' END nivel FROM membership.Users u LEFT JOIN incident.LPUser2 a ON a.UserID=u.IncidentUserID OUTER APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 x.UserID FROM incident.LPUser2 x WHERE x.LoginID=u.UserName OR x.EmailAddr=u.Email) b WHERE u.LastLoginDate>='2026-07-02' AND u.Email NOT LIKE '%@trebu.co' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM sso.SecurityLevelAssignments s WHERE s.UserName=u.UserName AND s.SecurityID>0)) t GROUP BY ruta,nivel;

SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT m.UserName) FROM sso.LocationHierarchyMembers m JOIN sso.PermissionGroups p ON p.UserName=m.UserName AND p.GroupName='ApprissCase Users' WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM place.Location l WHERE l.LocationID=m.LocationID);
```

## 4. Proposed split

| Issue | Type | Where it would live |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Slow load from Secure to Incident | performance | <custom data-type="smartlink" data-id="id-4">https://trebuco.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-9990</custom> , stays on this ticket |
| Level not applied at sign in, 46 users | sign in code | new RCS, Under Engineering Review |
| Office locations 9000xxxx missing, 287 users, plus the missing 2026-10-14 load | data | new RCS, Under Delivery Review |

## 5. Still open

1. Does finding 1 need an ENG ticket, or is there a support side fix for users without an LPUser2 row?
2. Is one RCS per cause the split you had in mind?
3. Should the 9000xxxx office locations load into `place.Location` for TBI, or should those users get a store assigned?

comments.body:
Hello,

Thank you for contacting Appriss Retail Support.

We’ve received your ticket and are routing it to the appropriate team for assistance. The assigned representative will follow up as soon as they’ve had a chance to review.

Kind Regards,

Appriss Retail Support

🤖 Talos triage · confidence: medium

**Talos can make mistakes. Please check important information.**

**Verdict**  
Nothing found so far points to a defect in Secure's report setup. The "Home Store Dept Name" column is read straight from the partner reference data, and the working partner (32164302) versus the affected one (37045592) looks like a difference in the data for that partner.

**What we checked**

## 1. Environment and steps to reproduce

**Production.** GP9 `ardm_112`, Snowflake `ARDMPROD.ARDM_112`, `\\dsprod1\retail\data\c112ahl\xml\error`, blob `stprdwus2shrdtlog/112ahl`.

1. Count `ardm_112.ardm_header` by minute of `endtransdatetime` for 2026-08-12 20:20 to 22:30.
2. Copy the six August zips from `xml\error` to a temp folder and decrypt them with `apprissgpg d c112ahl`.
3. List the XML names inside each zip. The first 12 digits are the transaction date and time.
4. Look up sample XML names in `ardm_header.filename`.

Expected: every XML from those zips present in `ardm_header`, and 1,000 to 2,000 transactions per minute on 8/12 evening. Actual: see findings.

## 2. Findings

1. **The 8/12 gap never reached us.** `ardm_header` is at zero from 20:34 to 20:36 and from 20:55 to 22:19. None of the six error zips holds a transaction stamped 8/12 21:00 to 22:59. GP9 and Snowflake match. Verified 9/24 and 9/25.
2. **Each error zip holds one or two XMLs filled with zero bytes.** That is the `ParseError: not well-formed (invalid token): line 1, column 0` in `ardm_prod_ardm_logs_base_20260814_002734.log` line 229. Verified 9/25.

| Error zip | XMLs | Transactions inside | Zero-filled XML |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 20260813211832251 | 15,684 | 8/11 20h and 21h, 8/12 20h | 2026081220490540041901601.xml |
| 20260815232950113 | 15,874 | 8/14 20h | 2026081420386054070202581.xml |
| 20260816135725133 | 6,523 | 8/11 18h and 19h | 2026081119012587040501481.xml, 2026081119012588003101041.xml |
| 20260816141814815 | 23,757 | 8/14 18h, 8/16 09h | 2026081418160637001400491.xml |
| 20260817143721575 | 40,668 | 8/13 22h and 23h | 2026081323002552053400021.xml |
| 20260817193820049 | 4,132 | 8/16 17h | 2026081617100638007701591.xml |

3. 15 of 18 sample XMLs are in `ardm_header`, loaded later on 8/15, 8/17, 8/26 and 8/27. Most of the error zip content came back through resends. Verified 9/25.
4. **Still missing:** `2026081609270072001200101.xml` and `2026081609346051040200201.xml` from zip 20260816141814815, both 8/16 09h. Also `2026081220490540041901601.xml`, the zero-filled one. Verified 9/25.

## 3. Troubleshooting performed, and the limits of support access

Claude proposed the checks and wrote the queries and scripts. I ran all of them myself on DEVWUS2DSM01 after running `env_setup.ps1` from appriss_pipeline: `apprissgpg i c112ahl`, `apprissgpg d c112ahl` on copies of the six zips, a Python listing of XML names, and a GP9 lookup of 18 sample names. The copies were deleted afterwards. Nothing in `xml\error` was moved or changed.

This is what I think is happening: `xml_ingest.py` walks the XMLs in name order and stops at the zero-filled one, so everything that sorts after it in that zip is lost. In zip 20260816141814815 the sample before the bad XML loaded and the two samples after it did not. Could someone else evaluate this and give me your thoughts?

The GP9 daily pipeline for c112ahl shows Disabled and Migrated To Snowflake since 9/3.

Outside the ticket: Teams thread in Retail Ops, Data Issues, 8/27. Guidance from Sebastian Rueda on `apprissgpg`. No calls.

## 4. Ruled out

| Hypothesis | Why |
| --- | --- |
| The 8/12 20:55 to 22:19 window is in an error zip | No error zip holds 8/12 21h or 22h |
| Fallback GPG setup failed caused the drops | It appears every night, including clean loads |
| Duplicate rows on 8/12 | 1,922,680 rows and 1,922,680 distinct filenames |

## 5. Still open

1. Could zip 20260816141814815 be reprocessed without the zero-filled XML, to recover 8/16 09h? Its first half is already loaded, so a skip on existing filenames would avoid duplicates.
2. Is the whole-zip drop on one bad XML, with a conditional success result, expected behavior? The error folder holds 86 zips since 7/6/2025.
3. With Ahold on Snowflake since 9/3, which path would that reprocess take?
